title: Every Man Struggling With Lust Needs This
paragraphs:
Every Man Struggling With Lust Needs This
The Battle You Hide Is Not the One That Will Destroy You. The Battle You Refuse to Bring to Jesus Is.
There are battles men rarely admit out loud.
Not because they do not know they are wrong.
But because shame has convinced them they are fighting alone.
Yet somewhere behind closed doors, late at night, when nobody is watching, another war begins.
You wonder if God is tired of forgiving you.
You begin avoiding prayer because you feel like a hypocrite.
You stop opening your Bible because every page seems to expose you.
You slowly convince yourself that maybe you're simply "that kind of Christian."
If that is where you are today, don't stop reading.
Because this article is not about making you feel worse.
It is about showing you something Satan desperately hopes you never understand.
Long before pornography existed on phones, before websites, before social media algorithms learned men's weaknesses, Scripture already exposed the real battlefield.
"But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart." (Matthew 5:28)
The Greek text uses the phrase:

πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτήν
(pros to epithymēsai autēn)
The verb ἐπιθυμέω (epithymeō) means far more than simply noticing beauty.
It means to desire, to covet, to long after something that God has not given you.
He was exposing a heart that consumes another person as an object rather than honoring them as someone made in God's image.
This is why lust feels so powerful.
And only Jesus reaches that deeply.
King David understood this battle more than most.
His adultery with Bathsheba led to deception, murder, broken families, national consequences, and lifelong grief.
David's greatest sin did not begin in a bedroom.
It began with an unchecked look.
"Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it." (Proverbs 4:23)
The Hebrew word translated "guard" is נָצַר (nāṣar).
It means to keep watch like a soldier protecting a city under attack.
Your heart was never designed to remain unguarded.
The apostle James explains exactly how temptation grows.
"Each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire. Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin when it is fully grown brings forth death." (James 1:14–15)
The enemy knows something many believers forget.
"If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness." (1 John 1:9)
The Greek word ὁμολογέω (homologeō) means to agree with, to acknowledge openly, to speak the same thing.
Confession is not informing God of something He does not know.
It is finally agreeing with Him.
"There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." (Romans 8:1)
Paul does not say there are no consequences for sin.
He says there is no condemnation for those who belong to Christ.
Conviction comes from the Holy Spirit.
The difference was not the size of their sin.
The difference was where they ran afterward.
Many men are trying to defeat lust by using more willpower.
Jesus never promised willpower would save you.
"Walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh." (Galatians 5:16)
The Greek word περιπατεῖτε (peripateite) literally means keep walking.
The Christian life is not built on one giant victory.
It is built on thousands of daily surrenders.
Maybe today your surrender looks like deleting an app.
Maybe it means ending a secret conversation.
Maybe it means installing accountability software.
Maybe it means confessing to a trusted brother in Christ.
Maybe it means removing entertainment that quietly feeds desires you later pretend appeared from nowhere.
Jesus spoke radically because sin is deadly.
"If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away." (Matthew 5:29)

Jesus was using deliberate hyperbole, not commanding literal self-harm. His point is unmistakable: deal decisively with whatever repeatedly leads you into sin. Remove the source rather than negotiating with it.
Perhaps the greatest lie men believe is this:
"I'll finally come to God after I get clean."
The Gospel says exactly the opposite.
Jesus did not die for future perfect versions of us.
"But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us."
The Hebrew idea of repentance is often connected with שׁוּב (shuv).
Repentance is not merely feeling guilty.
It is changing direction because Christ is worth following.
Every time you turn back to Jesus, heaven is not rolling its eyes.
The Father is still watching the road like the father in Luke 15, ready to embrace the returning son.
This is the scandal of grace.
The holy God we offended became the Savior who pursued us.
The Judge stepped into our sentence.
The Shepherd searched for wandering sheep.
The King wore a crown of thorns.
The innocent died for the guilty.
That is why our message has always been:
If you have fallen again, hear this carefully.
Your latest failure does not have the final sentence.
The cross does not excuse sin.
It destroys sin's ultimate claim over those who trust Christ.
But if your faith is in Christ alone, your hope has never rested in your flawless performance.
It has always rested in His finished work.
Today, stop making peace with hidden darkness.
If someone you love is silently battling lust, don't assume they already know this truth. Sometimes one shared message becomes the answer to someone else's prayer.
The greatest victory is not the day temptation disappears—it is the day you stop running from the Savior who never stopped running toward you.
